The required property $(x=a+b, y=b+c, z=c+a$ for distinct $a, b, c \in S)$ requires $x, y, z$ to have the same parity, and specifically, they must all be even for $a, b, c$ to be integers.

To construct a subset $A$ that avoids this property, we choose $A$ such that no triplet in $A$ consists of three even numbers. The simplest way to achieve this is to choose $A$ to be the set of all odd integers in $S$.

Let $A = S_{odd} = \{1, 3, 5, \ldots, 2023\}$.
$|A| = 2024 / 2 = 1012$.

Since all elements of $A$ are odd, for any $x, y, z \in A$, the required components $a, b, c$ cannot be integers (as $x+z-y$ would be odd), thus $A$ avoids the required property trivially.

This set $A$ of size 1012 provides a lower bound for $k$ (i.e., $k > 1012$).
